title: Living in Italy
lead: Finding a flat, avoiding scams, health, work and the first week: what students struggle with most, in plain language.

sections.title: Finding a flat
sections.intro: In big student cities (Milan, Bologna, Rome) finding housing is one of the hardest tasks. Start early: 2–3 months before classes begin.
items: Types: posto letto (a bed in a shared room), stanza singola (single room, shared kitchen), monolocale (studio flat).
First choice: the dormitory of the regional scholarship agency (DSU). If you are a scholarship winner, the place can be free or much cheaper. You apply together with the scholarship, in summer.
Check the university's housing office and its official notices page.
Groups of Uzbek and international students at the university help a lot. But be careful there too.
Book a temporary place (dormitory, hostel) for the first weeks after arrival. See the flat in person, then sign a contract.

sections.title: Avoiding scams
sections.intro: Where foreign students are most often cheated: fake listings asking for money in advance.
items: Do not transfer money without seeing the flat and signing a contract.
Do not trust a landlord who says «I am abroad, I will send the keys by post»: this is a classic scam.
If the price is much lower than nearby, that is a warning sign.
If you cannot go in person, ask for a live video call showing the flat.
Get a receipt for every payment. Pay by bank transfer, not cash.
Ask for the landlord's identity and proof that the flat belongs to them.

sections.title: Rental contract
sections.intro: An official, registered contract protects you and is also needed for the permesso and the scholarship.
items: There is a special contract type for students: «contratto per studenti universitari», from 6 months to 3 years (Law 431/1998, article 5).
The contract must be registered with the Agenzia delle Entrate. Ask for a copy.
For the «fuori sede» scholarship many regions require a paid, registered rental contract (for example in Padua for at least 10 months).
Check that the contract states the deposit and whether utilities (utenze) are included in the price.
Have the contract translated and understand it before signing.

sections.title: Health
sections.intro: For the permesso you need insurance for the whole period. There are two ways.
items: Voluntary registration with the Italian national health service (SSN): {{ssn}} per year for students, only per calendar year (January–December), not payable in instalments.
Or a private insurance policy valid in Italy.
If you register with the SSN, you choose a family doctor (medico di base) and get a tessera sanitaria (health card).
In an emergency: call 112. Pronto soccorso (emergency department) helps everyone.

sections.title: Working
sections.intro: You can work legally with a student permesso, but there is a limit.
items: You can work up to 20 hours a week (1 040 hours a year).
The employer must sign an official contract (contratto). Undeclared work can cause problems when renewing the permesso.
Universities offer paid part-time jobs for students (collaborazioni studentesche). Watch for notices on the university website.
Put your classes first: to keep the scholarship next year, you need credits (CFU).

sections.title: Difficulties: we speak honestly
sections.intro: Italy is beautiful, but the first year is not easy. If you know in advance, you will be ready.
items: Bureaucracy is slow: queues at the Questura, post office and bank can be long. Always carry copies of your documents.
You will need Italian in everyday life: even if your programme is in English, aim for A2–B1.
The scholarship is usually paid late and in instalments. Have your own money for the first 3–4 months.
Housing in big cities is expensive and scarce. Smaller university towns can be cheaper and more comfortable.
Loneliness and homesickness are natural. Student associations and university events help.

sections.title: First week: checklist
sections.intro: Do things in order from the day you arrive.
items: Days 1–8: hand in the post office kit for the permesso di soggiorno.
Get a codice fiscale (or it is issued at the permesso appointment).
Italian SIM card and bank account (IBAN): the scholarship is paid into it.
Hand in your original documents to the university and complete full enrollment.
Upload the permesso receipt and IBAN to the scholarship agency's portal.
Health: register with the SSN or check your insurance.
Get a student card and a transport pass.
